items.question: How did the diverse streams of tantra acquire multiple transmission identities?
premises: These streams have arrived at a condition.
That condition is the state of multiple transmissions.
items.inference: The diverse tantric streams have come to constitute multiple transmission traditions.
uncertainties: Whether āgatāḥ implies historical arrival or logical derivation is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: The various streams of tantra have attained the state of being multiple transmissions.

name of a goddess; form as given in text

items.question: Which divine forms are enumerated among the manifestations of the transmission?
premises: Maṅgalā is named as a form.
Mahāmāyā, Caṇḍā, and Kāpālinī are named as forms.
Śivā is named as a form.
items.inference: These goddesses constitute a set of named manifestations within the transmission.
uncertainties: The form caṇḍa may represent Caṇḍā with final vowel variation in the source.
items.plain_english: Maṅgalā, Mahāmāyā, Caṇḍā, Kāpālinī, and Śivā are named.

items.question: What additional divine forms continue the enumeration of the transmission?
premises: Anākhyā and Mahābhāṣā are named as forms.
Guhyakālī and Jayā are named as forms.
Parā is named as a supreme form.
items.inference: This verse extends the list of divine manifestations with further named forms.
uncertainties: Whether parā functions as an epithet of Jayā or as a separate name is ambiguous.
items.plain_english: Anākhyā, Mahābhāṣā, Guhyakālī, Jayā, and the supreme Parā are named.

items.question: Which further goddesses complete this sequence of named manifestations?

items.plain_english: Sundarī, Tripurā, Cāru, Ugracaṇḍā, and Prakāśinī are named.

items.question: How should the unity and multiplicity of the goddess be understood?
premises: This truth is to be known through the divine eye.
items.inference: One should recognize the goddess as simultaneously one and manifold through divine vision.
items.plain_english: One should know with the divine eye that she is one and also many-formed.

rows.grounds: compound anuṣṭhāna-rata describing one engaged in ritual practice
compound siddhi-bhāgin indicating attainment of accomplishment

items.question: What result follows for one devoted to ritual practice?
premises: A person may be devoted to practice.
Such devotion leads to participation in accomplishment.
This outcome is stated as certain.
items.inference: One devoted to practice certainly becomes a sharer in all accomplishment.
uncertainties: The scope of sarvaṃ as all accomplishments or all things is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: One devoted to practice would certainly become a sharer in all accomplishment.
